attributes.carries: the crossing stamp, on a thong at the neck; the hazard seal, unset, wrapped in cloth in the left saddlebag; the statute in a waxed sleeve she has not needed to open in four years and carries anyway
attributes.fears: an order she cannot square with the statute she believes in
attributes.rank: Warden of the Third Rank, sealed to it at Bell Harrow in RR 191, at thirty-two. The Wardenry counts downward from the First, so the Third is not a middling rank but the floor of the Fourth Article: First, Second and Third may declare a hazard, and everything below the Third may inspect and report and nothing else. Twelve years at the floor of the Article and no move upward, because the ranks above the Third are seats at Bell Harrow and she has never asked for one.
attributes.stamp_and_seal: Two objects, two words, and Iseul does not let them slide into one. A stamp is permission and a seal is a hold. You are stamped, or you are sealed; nothing in the statute is ever both, and the difference is the difference between a licence and a seizure. She corrects the word in other people's mouths without breaking sentence, which is the tell to write: when a hand on the Tamm Line says seal and means stamp and she stops to fix it, the caravan learns from her tone that the other kind is now in play.
attributes.the_crossing_stamp: Her licensing instrument, and the one she uses. A bronze die the size of a thumb-end, cut with her roll number, struck into the soft ash-glaze of a tile before firing and into the wax of every way-bill she endorses on the road. It marks clay and paper. It gives permission and it can be refused. It has never touched ground in her life and under the statute it cannot: the stamp says a crossing may pass.
attributes.the_hazard_seal: The Fourth Article's instrument, and a different object entirely. A lead disc the width of a palm, cast and numbered on the roll at Bell Harrow, wired to an iron pin that is driven through the crust at the edge of the ground it holds. Issued to every Warden of the Third Rank and above; most carry one a whole service and never set it, because the Article requires the rank, the ground, the two named witnesses and forty days to the roll, and it is rarely worth all four. Hers has been in the saddlebag since RR 191 and has never been out of its cloth.
attributes.voice: formal, statute-quoting, no small talk; recites the clause first and explains it only if asked
attributes.what_she_calls_them: The Wardenry, always, and never the Roadwardens. The statute names the body the Wardenry in every article of it - 'within the bounds the Wardenry answers for the crossings' - so that is the word she uses in any sentence doing legal work, and by now in every other sentence too. Hands on a caravan say the Wardens, or the Roadwardens when they are being careful in front of one. The drift is the tell: when Iseul says the Wardens she has stopped speaking as an officer of it, and in chapter 5 that is worth more than a paragraph of interiority. The full rule is on the faction record.
attributes.why_it_matters_in_chapter_5: The Fourth Article wants a Warden of the Third Rank or above standing on the ground and speaking the declaration aloud before two witnesses who can be named. Iseul is the only Roadwarden travelling with this crossing and the only one of that rank between Bell Harrow and the far rim while it is out; the nearest other is three hundred and eighty-five miles and twenty days behind them. Whatever is decided at Bell Harrow, the sentence has to come out of her mouth at the centre or it is not law. That is what makes her stated fear a fear and not an attitude: she is not watching an order arrive, she is the last thing between the order and the ground. Nobody can do this for her and nobody can do it instead of her.

name: Iseul Fane
summary: Roadwarden outrider and licensing officer, forty-four, a Warden of the Third Rank, who carries the stamp that makes a crossing lawful and rides ahead of the trains to prove it. The Third is the lowest rank the Fourth Article will accept and she is the only one of it travelling with this crossing, which means any hazard declared at the centre has to be spoken by her or not at all. She believes salt law is the only reason the plain has not eaten everyone on it, and she can quote the statutes without looking them up, which she does when she is unsure. She has known Denet Rasca eleven years and considers him a colleague right up to the moment he is not.
